sources.title: An Investigation into the Removal of Nine U.S. Attorneys in 2006 — Chapter Six
supports: the courthouse investigation began under the reviewed office and was assigned to a career prosecutor
political actors sought accelerated action before the election
the public record distinguishes investigative continuity from an indictment-ready decision
the successor had long served in senior office management
limits: does not publish an outgoing-to-successor handoff object
does not publish the contemporaneous prosecution memorandum or charging analysis

sources.title: Metropolitan Courthouse public-corruption indictment announcement
supports: the acting successor office announced a grand-jury indictment in the same courthouse matter
career prosecutors prepared and presented the evidence
three related guilty pleas had already been entered
federal and state investigative components continued the matter
limits: announcement issued after the personnel transition
does not identify a transferred memorandum or outgoing custodian receipt
indictment is an accusation rather than evidence of guilt

sources.title: United States v. Martinez et al. — Metropolitan Courthouse indictment
supports: a source-addressable charging object exists for the same matter after the transition
the indictment identifies the alleged conspiracy, mail-fraud, money-laundering, and forfeiture theories
the alleged conduct spans the period investigated by the predecessor office
limits: no direct handoff event is described
grand-jury charging does not reveal the predecessor's contemporaneous readiness judgment

sources.title: United States Supreme Court denies Toby Martinez petition for writ of certiorari
supports: one charged defendant later pleaded guilty
a prison sentence and restitution order were imposed
the Tenth Circuit affirmed the sentence
the Supreme Court denied certiorari
limits: later outcome for one defendant is not a direct handoff receipt
later success cannot be attributed to the predecessor without a transfer record
does not establish complete custody for every branch of the matter

sources.title: MSPB FOIA Program
supports: Board decisions are ordinarily posted publicly
initial decisions may require a FOIA request
case files may contain pleadings, hearing records, notices, orders, and decisions
limits: does not establish case status, final merits, or custody

sources.title: George W. Bush Presidential Library research and FOIA access
supports: textual, audiovisual, and electronic presidential records are held under the Presidential Records Act and FOIA
open records may be researched through finding aids, the research room, or reproduction routes
born-digital records may not be available online
limits: access route rather than evidence acquisition
White House records may clarify removal pressure but do not necessarily contain the prosecution handoff object
no request, reproduction order, or research-room review was executed
